children: A 94% gain in a single trading session is enough to turn heads. For one
, however, Friday’s explosive move in a tiny portfolio holding translated into something closer to a scratch-off jackpot.
Shares of
The Marygold Companies
jumped about 94% on Friday. Bloomberg Intelligence ETF analyst
Eric Balchunas
highlighted the move on X, noting that no ETF appears to have exposure to the stock, with the
EA Bridgeway Ultra-Small Company Market ETF
being the only exception.
I love the smell of a 91% gain in the morning.. I looked and no one owns this stock really, except
, the EA ultra small co ETF so congrats to them, albeit it was a tiny weighting = like when you win $25 on scratch-off lottery ticket at the gas station, not life changing but…
The catch? BUSM’s position was tiny.
Marygold’s latest available ownership data showed BUSM holding 54,039 shares, equivalent to about 0.05% of MGLD’s outstanding stock.

That means Friday’s 94% surge would add only about $50,800 to a position of that size, assuming the holding remained unchanged. Against a diversified portfolio, the impact is therefore modest — exactly the kind of “nice, but not life-changing” gain Balchunas was getting at.
Trading volume of MGLD shares on Friday reached an impressive 13.1 million shares, indicating heightened interest and participation in the stock, according to

. MGLD’s fundamentals provide some additional context for why the stock has been attracting attention. The company reported 8% fiscal 2026 revenue growth to $25.3 million, while its USCF Investments business posted 23% revenue growth. Average assets under management at the fund-management business rose 41% to $4.1 billion.

The episode also illustrates the peculiar math of ultra-small-cap ETFs. A position representing only a fraction of a percent can suddenly become one of the portfolio’s biggest percentage winners when an obscure microcap doubles in a day.
For BUSM, Friday brought the fireworks. The position, however, was small enough that the champagne probably came in a miniature bottle.
